sn35.93:1.1: “Bhikkhus, consciousness comes to be in dependence on a dyad.
sn35.93:1.2: And how, bhikkhus, does consciousness come to be in dependence on a dyad?
sn35.93:1.3: In dependence on the eye and forms there arises eye-consciousness.
sn35.93:1.4: The eye is impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise;
sn35.93:1.5: forms are impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:1.6: Thus this dyad is moving and tottering, impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:1.8: The cause and condition for the arising of eye-consciousness is also impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:1.9: When, bhikkhus, eye-consciousness has arisen in dependence on a condition that is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.93:1.10: “The meeting, the encounter, the concurrence of these three things is called eye-contact.
sn35.93:1.11: Eye-contact too is impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:1.12: The cause and condition for the arising of eye-contact is also impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:1.13: When, bhikkhus, eye-contact has arisen in dependence on a condition that is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.93:1.14: “Contacted, bhikkhus, one feels, contacted one intends, contacted one perceives.
sn35.93:1.15: Thus these things too are moving and tottering, impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:2.1: “In dependence on the ear and sounds there arises ear-consciousness …
sn35.93:3.1: In dependence on the mind and mental phenomena there arises mind-consciousness.
sn35.93:3.2: The mind is impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise;
sn35.93:3.3: mental phenomena are impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.4: Thus this dyad is moving and tottering, impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.6: The cause and condition for the arising of mind-consciousness is also impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.7: When, bhikkhus, mind-consciousness has arisen in dependence on a condition that is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.93:3.8: “The meeting, the encounter, the concurrence of these three things is called mind-contact.
sn35.93:3.9: Mind-contact too is impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.10: The cause and condition for the arising of mind-contact is also impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.11: When, bhikkhus, mind-contact has arisen in dependence on a condition that is impermanent, how could it be permanent?
sn35.93:3.12: “Contacted, bhikkhus, one feels, contacted one intends, contacted one perceives.
sn35.93:3.13: Thus these things too are moving and tottering, impermanent, changing, becoming otherwise.
sn35.93:3.14: “It is in such a way, bhikkhus, that consciousness comes to be in dependence on a dyad.”
